descriptive_title: Grade 2 Mathematics: Algebra (Coding) — Conditional Statements and Code Reading Without Screens (C3.1-C3.2)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.C3.1: solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves conditional statements and other control structures
curriculum_expectations.C3.2: read and alter existing code, including code that involves conditional statements and other control structures, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 2 unit on coding without screens (C3.1-C3.2) framed around 'If-Then Detectives' — Inspector If the Conditional Cat and her partner Then the Action Dog. Day 1 introduces conditional statements: 'IF X happens, THEN do Y'. Day 2 writes IF-THEN code for math situations. Day 3 reads existing IF-THEN code and predicts outcomes. Day 4 alters IF-THEN code and describes effects. Day 5 closes with child-invented IF-THEN projects. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough covering common Grade-2 misconceptions: the always-true trap, the missed branch trap, the alteration-doesn't-matter trap. The unit progresses concrete (physical IF-THEN sorting) → representational (code cards with IF-THEN) → abstract (multi-conditional code).
unit_learning_goal: Children will write and execute code with conditional statements; read and alter existing IF-THEN code; and describe how changes to the conditions affect the outcomes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: An IF-THEN statement says: IF a condition is true, THEN do an action. Real-life examples: IF it rains, THEN take an umbrella.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can read an IF-THEN statement and explain what it means.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Inspector If sorts everyday IF-THEN statements; children create their own.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can write IF-THEN code for math: IF the number is even, THEN clap. IF the number is odd, THEN stomp.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can write IF-THEN code for a math situation.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children write IF-THEN code for sorting tasks (even/odd, big/small) using code cards.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Reading IF-THEN code means following the condition and predicting the action. We trace the code with example values.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can read IF-THEN code and predict the outcome.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children trace existing IF-THEN code with sample inputs and predict outputs.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Changing the condition or the action changes the outcome. IF X, THEN Y becomes IF X, THEN Z — the action changes.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can alter IF-THEN code and describe the effect.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children alter existing IF-THEN code (change condition, change action, swap branches) and predict the effect.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can write our own IF-THEN code for a math task in our life. Sort, classify, decide, repeat.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can write my own IF-THEN code for a math task.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children invent a math sorting task with IF-THEN code; gallery walk and share.

recurring_characters.name: Inspector If the Conditional Cat
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A friendly cat detective with a notebook for sorting IF cases. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A friendly cat with a deerstalker cap, notebook, and a magnifying glass. Cheerful expression, striped tail, alert ears.

recurring_characters.name: Then the Action Dog
recurring_characters.role: Inspector If's action partner. The 'do-the-thing' character. Cameo Lessons 2-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: An eager dog with a tool belt and a bandana. Tongue out, tail wagging. Holds an action card.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: Something that is either TRUE or FALSE. The IF part of an IF-THEN.
Something we DO. The THEN part of an IF-THEN.
A code statement. IF a condition is TRUE, THEN do the action.
When something is the case. The condition is TRUE means it happened.
When something is NOT the case. The condition is FALSE means it didn't happen.
What HAPPENS as a result of the code. The outcome is the action that ran.
To CHANGE something. We alter code by changing a condition or an action.

assessment_strategy.diagnostic: Lesson 1 IF-THEN snapshot: each child reads 4 IF-THEN statements and labels them TRUE or FALSE for given inputs. Tally accuracy.
assessment_strategy.formative: Lesson 2 writing tracker; Lesson 3 reading tracker; Lesson 4 altering tracker.
assessment_strategy.summative: Lesson 5 IF-THEN Project worksheet — children invent a math IF-THEN code. Captures C3.1 + C3.2 in one creative artifact.

pedagogical_notes: C3.1 with conditionals adds a new layer beyond Grade-1 sequencing. Children must check the condition before running the action.
C3.2 reading must include tracing — substitute an input value, check the condition, run the matching action.
The TRUE/FALSE distinction is foundational. Use the sorting mat throughout.
Avoid overly complex conditions in Grade 2. Stick to single conditions (even/odd, big/small, more-than-N).
Real-life IF-THENs (umbrella, traffic light) ground the abstract syntax.
canadian_context_notes: Real-life examples: IF it snows, THEN wear boots. IF the Leafs win, THEN cheer. IF the Tim Hortons line is long, THEN order ahead.
Hockey rules as IF-THEN: IF a player scores, THEN add 1 to the team's score. IF the goalie catches it, THEN no goal.
Toonie/loonie examples: IF you have 2 toonies, THEN you have $4.
